citation.sourceDocument: Michigan Department of Treasury Form 446 (Rev. 02-26), 2026 Michigan Income Tax Withholding Guide — "Withholding Rate: 4.25% Personal Exemption Amount: $5,900"
citation.sourceNote: Michigan levies a single flat rate of 4.25% on Michigan taxable income (MCL 206.51). The rate carries a statutory trigger that cuts it for one year whenever general-fund revenue grows faster than inflation; that trigger fired once, for tax year 2023 (4.05%), and the rate returned to 4.25% for 2024 and has stayed there. There is no Michigan standard deduction. Instead each filer claims a PERSONAL EXEMPTION, indexed annually: Form 446, the 2026 Withholding Guide, states the 2026 figures on its first line — "Withholding Rate: 4.25% Personal Exemption Amount: $5,900" (up from $5,800 for 2025). This shard carries $5,900 single and head of household, $11,800 married filing jointly for two exemptions. Worked example, single $60,000: taxable = 60,000 − 5,900 = $54,100; tax = 4.25%·54,100 = $2,299.25. Omitted at launch fidelity: the $5,900-per-dependent exemption and the additional special exemptions (age 65+, blind, disabled, certain veterans); the retirement and pension subtraction, which the 2023 phase-in has grown large — for 2026, recipients born after 1945 may generally subtract up to $67,610 single or $135,220 joint; the Homestead Property Tax Credit and Home Heating Credit; and MICHIGAN CITY INCOME TAXES, which 24 cities levy on residents (Detroit at 2.4%, most others at 1%) and which this engine does not model — a Detroit resident therefore owes materially more than the figure shown here. Verified against Michigan Department of Treasury Form 446 (Rev. 02-26), the 2026 Michigan Income Tax Withholding Guide, on 2026-08-29.
